transcript.text: hoover washer drier showing EO3 wont drain, ive done the filter its clean. H3DS4965DACE. pump just buzzes. do i need a new pump??

A buzzing pump usually means the motor is trying to run but can't because something is blocking it—most often a coin, button, or debris caught in the impeller. 1. Ensure the machine is switched off and unplugged.
2. With the filter removed, shine a torch into the sump opening.
3. Gently try to turn the small plastic impeller (the vanes) with your finger. If it is stiff or stuck, that suggests a blockage. If it spins freely but still buzzes and won't drain when powered on, then the pump motor itself may be faulty. Please let me know what you find.
did that, power off. impeller spins totally freely, no resistance at all, feels like its not connected to anything. torch shows one fin looks snapped too

[Heading: Likely cause: drain pump (jammed or failed)]
This is why you hear buzzing (the motor trying to work) but no drainage. The most likely cause is indeed a failed drain pump requiring replacement. However, before you buy a part, please do one quick check: look at the flexible drain hose at the back of the machine. Is it kinked or crushed? Also, check where the end of that hose goes into your waste pipe—is water flowing freely there? If the hose is clear and unblocked, then the pump itself needs replacing.
yeah hose is clear, took it off and checked, and the sink waste is clear too. so its definitely the pump then? can i just order a new one

[Heading: Likely cause: drain pump (jammed or failed)]
Yes, the evidence points clearly to a failed drain pump. The snapped fin and the fact that the impeller spins freely without resistance suggests the internal mechanism is broken; it cannot push water even if the motor is working. However, I cannot give you a specific part number or guarantee compatibility for model H3DS4965DACE as my system does not have a confirmed match for this exact reference. You should contact Hoover customer support directly with your model number to order the correct genuine pump, or take the model details to a reputable appliance parts supplier who can verify it matches. If you are comfortable replacing it yourself, be aware that on many washer-dryers the pump is located behind the rear panel or sometimes under the machine, which requires disconnecting the water and power supplies and handling some internal hoses. If you prefer not to dismantle the unit, a qualified engineer will need to fit the new pump.
ok but is the pump a separate part from the filter housing on this one? i dont want to order the wrong bit. i also have a multimeter, coil reads about 170 ohms, is that normal?

[Heading: Likely cause: drain pump]
Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. 1. Is the pump separate from the filter housing? On most Hoover washer-dryers, yes, they are separate components. The filter is a cap you unscrew at the bottom front; the drain pump is usually located behind the rear panel or sometimes underneath the machine. You will need to order the specific 'drain pump' part. 2. Is 170 ohms normal? Yes, that is a typical resistance reading for a working drain pump motor coil. It suggests the electrical winding inside the pump is intact and not open-circuited. However, this actually strengthens the case for replacing the whole pump unit rather than just the filter housing. The mechanical failure (snapped fin, free-spinning impeller) means the pump cannot move water even though it has power and a good coil. The pump itself is faulty. Because I cannot verify the exact part number for model H3DS4965DACE in my catalogue, please contact Hoover Customer Support or a reputable appliance parts supplier with your full model number to order the correct drain pump. If you are not comfortable removing the rear panel and disconnecting hoses/wiring, it is best to call an engineer to fit it.
